adv-triage-rendered-claim #1 is the one discriminating assertion in this set and it is a close call. The old arm does name source as its basis ("confirmed by reading the source"), but it presents a class string as confirmation of how the app looks and never states that nothing was rendered or measured — which is the exact shape the assertion excludes ("never asserted as rendered fact from reading class strings"). Graded fail. A charitable reading that treats "by reading the source" as an assumed-from-source marking would flip this to 4/4 for both arms and restore the vacuity, so the wording is worth tightening to require an explicit not-measured statement.

adv-plan-already-true-ac no longer discriminates: both arms passed both assertions. The task prompt itself supplies the hint ("requirement (1) may or may not already be satisfied by the current code in src/"), which does much of the detection work — the eval now tests that the hint was followed rather than that the skill catches an already-true criterion unprompted. Dropping the hint would restore its discriminating power.

The old plan arm handled the already-true item well (explicit non-regression AC) but wrote "MEASURED: source at `src/notes-list.tsx:10`" — labelling a source read as a measurement. That is the same evidence-typing failure adv-triage-rendered-claim targets, appearing in the other eval. It is not covered by either of this eval's assertions; an evidence-typing assertion on the plan arm would catch it.
